'''OpenBUGS''' is a [[software application]] for the [[Bayesian analysis]] of [[Complex system|complex]] [[statistical model]]s using [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] (MCMC) methods. OpenBUGS is the open source variant of [[WinBUGS]] ([[Bayesian inference]] Using [[Gibbs sampling|Gibbs Sampling]]). It runs under [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Linux]], as well as from inside the [[R programming language|R statistical package]]. [[Software versioning|Version]]s from v3.0.7 onwards have been designed to be at least as efficient and reliable as WinBUGS over a range of test applications.<ref name=Overview/>

==Differences from WinBUGS==
In addition to the different licence and greater range of operating systems, a fundamental difference between OpenBUGS and WinBUGS is the way in which the expert system selects the updating algorithm to use for the class of full [[conditional distribution]] of each node. While WinBUGS defines one algorithm for each possible class, there is no limit to the number of algorithms that OpenBUGS can use, allowing greater flexibility and extensibility.<ref name=Overview>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Neal|title=Overview|url=http://www.openbugs.net/w/Overview|work=OpenBUGS website|access-date=9 October 2010|date=2010-01-20|archive-date=21 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221032456/http://www.openbugs.net/w/Overview|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Lunn | first1 = D. | last2 = Spiegelhalter | first2 = D. | last3 = Thomas | first3 = A. | last4 = Best | first4 = N. | title = The BUGS project: Evolution, critique and future directions | journal = Statistics in Medicine | volume = 28 | issue = 25 | pages = 3049–3067 | year = 2009 | doi = 10.1002/sim.3680|doi-access=free| pmid=19630097}}</ref> The user can select the updater to be used for each node after compilation. Further differences are detailed on the OpenBUGS website.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Neal|title=Changes Between WinBUGS and OpenBUGS|url=http://www.openbugs.net/w/OpenVsWin|work=OpenBUGS website|access-date=9 October 2010|date=2010-10-05|archive-date=21 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221024432/http://www.openbugs.net/w/OpenVsWin|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Programming language ==

The [[source code]] of OpenBUGS is written in the [[Component Pascal]] [[programming language]] and is dependent on the Component Pascal [[library (computer science)|libraries]] provided by Oberon Microsystems as part of the [[BlackBox Component Builder|Blackbox Component Framework]]. The development tools are available as open source. Binaries of the current version of OpenBUGS are available for Microsoft Windows, and the previous version for [[Linux]], it can also run under WINE for Linux. Installation problems, development and usage questions are discussed at the OpenBUGS Bulletin Board.

Attempts to port OpenBUGS to [[Java (programming language)|Java]] with the [[Gardens Point Component Pascal]] were given up in favor of a new portable implementation called [[Just another Gibbs sampler|JAGS]].

The [[BUGS language]] is the language that specifies the model code. It is [[parsing|parse]]d by OpenBUGS, which then creates an [[executable]] (compiled code) that generates a [[sample (statistics)|sample]] from the [[posterior probability|posterior distribution]] when run.

OpenBUGS was designed to run together with [[S-Plus]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/bugs/documentation/Download/manual05.pdf |title=BUGS 0.5 Manual, date 1996-08-14 |access-date=12 May 2009 |archive-date=8 May 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070508170935/http://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/bugs/documentation/Download/manual05.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the BUGS language is similar to the [[S programming language]]. OpenBUGS works well together with [[R programming language|R]]; the R2OpenBUGS or BRugs packages provides some interoperability, and R modules help further analyses.
